summary: Ko T T1c: an app where users upload photo(s) and receive high-quality, realistic image outputs; pivot requested from single-photo semantic outfit/background variations to a two-photo "fusion/collision" workflow that blends two photographs into a new variation while preserving quality and brand intro/manifesto experience.
architectural_notes: Image generation must preserve the subject identity from the uploaded photo while modifying only allowed attributes (e.g., outfit/background) in a realistic style.

Landing/intro experience must display the newly provided introduction letter text (Subject: “Strength in Numbers (and a Weakness in Yours)” through the closing Ko T T1C tagline) in full at the top of the page, exactly as written (including the Louis Vuitton URL).
Generated variations should include substantive styling/wardrobe changes (e.g., outfit type/shape and color) rather than simple image adjustments (hue/contrast).
Support a two-photo input pipeline (upload/preview two images) for a "fusion/collision" generation mode that blends the photos into a new output rather than applying simple global edits.
“Fusion/collision” must follow the common meaning of fusing two inputs into one blended/combined output derived from BOTH photos (not a single-photo edit mislabeled as fusion).
known_issues: User feedback: current variations may resemble simple edits (hue/contrast) rather than true outfit/style changes; needs improvement to meet 'actual variations' expectation.
Reported behavior: generator produces no meaningful variation (output remains essentially identical aside from temperature/color shift), failing the expected variation behavior.

existing_features.title: Create a landing/intro experience for “Ko T T1C — The Chaos That Finally Makes Sense” that displays the full provided introduction/manifesto text and the provided tagline exactly as written, in English, within the app UI.
Implement a photo submission flow where a user can upload a single photo (JPG/PNG) and preview it before generating variations.

Generate multiple “variations” from the uploaded photo that preserve the original person/identity (i.e., do not alter facial features/body identity) while varying only background and/or overall styling in a realistic, high-quality manner using an on-device image processing pipeline (no external AI services).
Add a “quality guard” UX for outputs: allow the user to flag a generated variation as “bad/distorted,” hide it from the main grid, and regenerate a replacement variation using a different preset.
Persist a lightweight history of user submissions (original + generated variations + timestamps) so a user can revisit previous sessions from within the app.
Choose and apply a coherent visual theme for Ko T T1c and enforce it consistently across the landing, upload, generation, and history views.
Add static branding imagery to the UI by including the user-provided Ko T T1c images as visible brand elements (e.g., hero/cover and/or logo placement) without requiring backend image routing.

Update the landing/intro page to display the user-provided introduction letter in full, in English, at the very top of the page content (above the existing manifesto content), preserving the wording, punctuation, and paragraph/line breaks as provided. The text must include the “Subject: Strength in Numbers (and a Weakness in Yours)” line and the “Dear Louis Vuitton (https://www.louisvuitton.com),” line.

Update the on-device variation generator so that generated results are meaningful, visually distinct variations (e.g., different outfit colors and different outfit shapes such as shorts-to-dress-like silhouettes) rather than primarily global hue/contrast/brightness edits.

Extend the variation preset system to support “semantic-style” variation types (e.g., outfit recolor, garment pattern overlay, garment silhouette warp, background swap/scene styling) and ensure the generator can pick from these types when creating variations and when regenerating a hidden/bad variation.

Update the generation UI copy in the Upload/Generate view to set user expectations that variations aim for outfit/style changes (color and shape) rather than simple photo edits, using English user-facing text.

Update the Upload/Generate experience to support selecting and previewing TWO input photos (Photo A and Photo B) before generation, including the ability to remove/replace either photo, and disable generation until both photos are provided.

Replace the current single-photo variation generation pipeline with an on-device two-photo “fusion/collision” generator that produces outputs derived from BOTH input photos, avoiding results that are effectively identical to one input with only minor temperature/color shifts.

Update the results management UX (grid, hide, and regenerate replacement) to work with fusion outputs, ensuring that regenerating a hidden/bad result generates a new fusion output based on the same two input photos (and does not revert to single-photo presets).

Update history persistence and history display to store and show both fusion input photos (Photo A and Photo B) alongside the generated outputs, including backward compatibility for existing single-photo history entries.

Update all user-facing copy in the Upload/Generate page to describe the new two-photo fusion workflow in English (remove/replace references to ‘outfit variations’ generated from a single photo where they no longer apply).

Update the on-device fusion generator so outputs are true fusions derived from BOTH Photo A and Photo B (a combined composite/collage/merge), not primarily global color adjustments or a simple uniform overlay; ensure the generator frequently exchanges/merges localized structures/textures between the two inputs (e.g., patch-based region mixing + edge-aware blending) so the result visibly contains meaningful elements from each input.

Add an on-device “both-inputs” contribution guard to detect and prevent outputs that are effectively identical to just Photo A or just Photo B (aside from minor global color/contrast changes); when detected, automatically retry with a different fusion recipe/seed until a maximum retry count is reached, then show a clear English error message if it cannot produce a valid fusion.

Update Upload/Generate page user-facing copy to define “fusion” in plain English as a combined result derived from BOTH photos (not a filter), and align button/section descriptions accordingly without introducing new workflow steps.

new_feature_requests.summary: Allow users to submit/upload a photo as input for generation
Generate multiple realistic photo variations that stay true to the uploaded person (preserve identity/model) while varying outfit and/or background
Quality/safety constraint: outputs must be high quality and realistic; avoid distorted/anatomically incorrect results (e.g., 'third leg' artifacts)
Include the provided full introduction/manifesto text and tagline in the app experience
Ensure generated 'variations' are meaningful semantic changes (e.g., different outfit colors/styles/shapes such as shorts→dress), not mere photo edits like hue/contrast adjustments
Replace/augment single-photo variations with a two-photo "fusion" mode: user uploads two photos to be collided/blended into a new variation output
